title: Quetzalcoatl
subtitle: The Feathered Serpent
subject: mythologie
description: Quetzalcoatl, the Feathered Serpent, is the god of Mesoamerican civilization. Its myth combines creation, exile and the fatal meeting with Cortés.

hero.hook: God, king and prophecy: the Feathered Serpent spans two thousand years of Mexican history.

blocks.text: **Quetzalcoatl**, the “Feathered Serpent”, is one of the richest figures in pre-Columbian Mexico. He has been venerated for more than two millennia, from , a large city on the central plateau, to the Aztecs, and among the Mayans under the name . [[Teotihuacán]] [[Kukulkán]]
He unites the earth (the serpent) and the sky (the feather). God of civilization, knowledge and moral order, his myth ends up intersecting with real history: the Spanish conquest of **1519**.
In , **[[quetzal]]coatl** comes from , the bird with green feathers, and *coatl*, the snake. This union makes it the bridge between the human and the divine. [[Nahuatl]]

blocks.caption: Quetzalcoatl, the Feathered Serpent: earth and sky intertwined.

blocks.text: In , he descends to , the world of the dead, to collect the bones of past humans. He brings them back to life with his blood. Then he steals **corn** from the ants: the founding food of Mexico. As god of the wind, he also opens the way for the rains of . [[Cosmogony of the five suns]] [[Mictlán]] [[Tlaloc]]
The quetzal's tail feathers can measure **60 cm**. Among the Mayans and Aztecs, killing the bird was punishable by death: a few feathers were taken from it, then released.

The myth also has a historical face: **Topiltzin Quetzalcoatl**, king-priest of **Tula** in the 10th century. He would have wanted to reform the cult and replace human sacrifices with offerings of flowers and butterflies.

blocks.caption: Tula, Toltec city linked to the reign and fall of Quetzalcoatl.

blocks.text: His rival **Tezcatlipoca** pushes him to drink pulque, a fermented drink. Humiliated, the king exiled to the east. According to legend, he promises to return one year “Un Reed”. This promise will carry weight.
After his departure, Quetzalcoatl sometimes becomes the Morning Star: the planet Venus. The god does not die, he changes form.

In **1519**, **Hernán Cortés** arrives in the east, the year “A Reed” of the Aztec calendar, the one in which the return of the god was expected. Emperor **Moctezuma II** hesitates: should we fight an invader or welcome a divinity?

blocks.caption: 1519: the arrival of Cortés meets the promise of divine return.

blocks.text: He sends gifts of gold and feathers. The [[Conquistadors]] see it as an invitation. The myth, true or amplified after the fact, becomes a psychological weapon in the fall of, the Aztec capital. [[Tenochtitlán]]

events.title: Creator
events.detail: Bones of the dead, divine blood, gift of corn.

blocks.text: After the conquest, Quetzalcoatl did not disappear. Some monks believe they see an apostle there. Later, independent Mexico made it an emblem of pre-Columbian greatness. 20th century muralists, like Diego Rivera, paint it as the soul of the country.
Even today, the Feathered Serpent expresses an identity: roots in the earth, ambition turned towards the sky.
**Quetzalcoatl**, Feathered Serpent, is the god of Mesoamerican civilization. Creator, exiled king, then fatal prophecy in **1519**, he remains a central symbol of Mexico.
